newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - UK stock options sold as shares weaken.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - UK stock options sold as shares weaken.

text.p: Traders took the opportunity to sell stock options on Monday as the London stock market drifted back, dealers said.
By early afternoon, the main trades came from sellers of retail and pharmaceuticals group Boots and in British Airways.
In Boots, 500 April 650 calls were sold at 27p which will make a maximum profit if the underlying shares are below 650p at expiry.
Profits will reduce to zero if the stock reaches 677p, but above 650p there is a risk of being assigned the calls.
If assigned, the options seller will have to sell 500,000 Boots' shares at 650p each.
By 1415 GMT, the shares were up 1-1/2p at 648-1/2p.
Over in British Airways, the main deal was the sale of 400 April 600 calls at 23p. The underlying shares fell 5-1/2p to 586p.
Elsewhere, puts and calls were sold in shipping and transportation group Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co in a short strangle strategy.
It involved selling 250 May 600 puts at 22p as well as 250 May 650 calls at 18p.
For maximum profit of 40p at expiry, the deal relies on P&O shares staying between 600p and 650p.
P&O shares shed a penny to 623p.
In the FTSE 100 index options, most of the activity was inspired by traders having differing views of market volatility and this led to some two-way trading in the out-of-the-money FTSE options.
By 1415 GMT, the FTSE was down 12.2 at 4,195.5.
